key_insight: Conditional Flow Matching can generate plausible 3D instantaneous urban wind and temperature fields from building geometry and mean flow, capturing turbulent variability rather than only deterministic averages.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, turbulence-aware urban microclimate prediction for design iteration, local gust assessment, and climate adaptation without the full cost of LES.
method: Uses Conditional Flow Matching as a generative surrogate for 3D velocity and temperature fields.
Conditions on building geometry and mean-flow inputs to guide physically plausible instantaneous field synthesis.
Uses overlapping pixel-space generation with shared-noise initialization to reduce GPU memory load while preserving spatial continuity.
evidence_signal: Against LES reference data, the model reported NRMSE of 2.99% for wind and 1.77% for temperature first-order statistics, 7.17% and 8.84% for second-order turbulence metrics, and about 7% for turbulent kinetic energy, while also matching PDFs and vertical profiles.
watch_item: Because the approach generates full 3D fields in pixel space, careful handling of overlap, noise sharing, and generalization to unseen urban geometries will be important.
paper_title: Conditional Flow Matching for Generation of 3D Multi-variable Instantaneous Urban Microclimate Fields
